title: Construction Dust Near Active Corridors: What Ends Up in HVAC Returns
headline: Gypsum fines, traffic film, and why stacked laundry closets stay hot
description: How nearby construction and corridor traffic can load returns with fine dust — practical signs to watch before you schedule a duct or dryer vent cleaning.

sections.heading: Downtown Herndon is quiet. The air west of it is not.
paragraphs: Elden Street and the municipal clock tower still look like a small town. A few blocks out, Worldgate and Herndon Parkway shift to townhomes. West toward Dulles, data-center pads and office builds keep a gypsum and soil film in the air for years. Returns do not wait for the last crane to leave.

Downtown brick cottages often run original trunks plus a later addition. Occupied streets next to active lots pull insulation fibers the same week they pull oak pollen. You change the filter. The registers still look like a job site.

sections.heading: Worldgate dryer runs fail in a specific way
paragraphs: Stacked Worldgate laundry closets send lint on a long path to a shared wall or roof cap. Construction dust in the ducts plus a packed dryer vent is how a closet stays humid all summer. The machine is usually fine. The vent is not.
